title: Islands of stars in the river
caption: Barred spiral galaxy NGC 1345, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 1345 · constellation Eridanus · about 85 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The loose, ragged arms of the spiral galaxy NGC 1345 fill this Hubble image, and all around it are more distant galaxies of many shapes and sizes, some even shining through the foreground galaxy. An elongated bar stretches out from its nucleus, with spiral arms reaching outward from it, which makes NGC 1345 a barred spiral.

The galaxy belongs to the Eridanus Galaxy Cluster, which gathers about 70 galaxies some 85 million light-years away in Eridanus, the River. The Fornax Cluster looks close by on the sky, though the two are really about 20 million light-years apart. Together they are called the Fornax or Southern Supercluster.

Sorting galaxies by shape tells astronomers a great deal about how the Universe has evolved, and people turn out to be better at recognising shapes than computers. That is why the citizen-science project Galaxy Zoo: Hubble has invited the public to help classify galaxies in Hubble's archive.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.91 x 1.60 arcminutes) and distance (85 million light years), the frame spans roughly 72,000 × 40,000 light-years. Its light set out about 85 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image was made with the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. Light through a blue filter (F435W) is shown in blue and light through a near-infrared filter (F814W) in red.
understand.eye: The red channel is near-infrared light, invisible to the eye, and the exposures, 17.5 minutes per filter, gather far more light than an eye could.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: John Herschel discovered NGC 1345 in 1835 while observing from South Africa. He called it small and very faint, and even today it shows up as only a small, round fuzz in a fairly large amateur telescope.
alt: A spiral galaxy with a central bar and loose, ragged arms, surrounded by many more distant galaxies of different shapes and sizes.
